target.title: feat(diagnostics-otel): identify each instance with service.instance.id
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In a multi-pod / multi-replica deployment, every OpenClaw process exports OTel telemetry under the same identity. The resource only carried `service.name`, with no `service.instance.id`, so collectors and backends cannot tell instances apart — per-pod metrics and traces collapse into one series.

## Approach (reworked after review)

An earlier revision added a custom `OTEL_SERVICE_INSTANCE_ID` env var with an `os.hostname()` fallback. Review correctly flagged that as a security-boundary concern (host identity exported by default) and a non-standard, non-unique default. This revision addresses all of that:

- Resolve `service.instance.id` with precedence: `diagnostics.otel.serviceInstanceId` config field → `OTEL_SERVICE_INSTANCE_ID` env var → **omitted entirely**.
- **No hostname fallback.** When neither source is set, the attribute is not added to the resource, so no host/pod identity is ever exported by default.
- Mirrors how `service.name` is already resolved (config field + env fallback), so it introduces no novel contract — just a symmetric, opt-in identity field.
- Operators who prefer the standard path can still use `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.instance.id=...`.

Docs (`docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md`) document the config field, env var, precedence, and the privacy note (opt-in, opaque, stable, never hostname).

## User Impact

Operators can opt into per-instance identity by setting a stable, opaque id (e.g. a provisioned pod UID) via config or env. Everyone else is unaffected — no attribute is added and no host identity is exposed. No migration required.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof** — the exact resolution + `resourceFromAttributes(...)` logic exercised against the real `@opentelemetry/resources` and `@opentelemetry/semantic-conventions` packages (no mocks), printing the final exported resource attributes for all four cases:

```
1) nothing set
   service.name        = openclaw
   service.instance.id = (absent)
2) config serviceInstanceId set
   service.name        = openclaw
   service.instance.id = pod-config-1
3) OTEL_SERVICE_INSTANCE_ID set
   service.name        = openclaw
   service.instance.id = pod-env-2
4) both set (config wins)
   service.name        = openclaw
   service.instance.id = pod-config-wins
```

This confirms: (1) absent by default (no hostname), (2) config value applied, (3) env value applied, (4) config takes precedence over env.

- `extensions/diagnostics-otel` test suite: **111 passed**, including 4 new tests (omit-by-default, config field, env var, config-wins precedence).
- Branch merged with latest `main` (previous merge conflict resolved).
